claims.statement: ParticipationTrigger is the only place an untagged message becomes a candidate for an unprompted turn: Dispatcher.on_message hands it a message only when ingest returned engage=False with relevance_gate=True, and any resulting turn goes through FirePath.speak rather than EngagementPipeline.

A room opts in to unprompted speech in policy.toml with relevance_gate = true on its [[conversations]] entry (default False), read by RelevanceGatePolicy, which is appended last to the engage chain only when [relevance_gate] enabled so a real tag keeps its own reason.

Participation ships inert and needs both [participation] enabled and [relevance_gate] enabled: Config refuses to start with a gate and no participation turn behind it, and with participation on but the gate off the composition root logs an error because no window is ever noted, judged or turned into a turn.

The composition root constructs ParticipationTrigger only when [relevance_gate] enabled and a FirePath exists, giving it fire_path.speak as a bound method and the same ConversationSlots every other path into that conversation holds.

A participation window closes on whichever arm comes first: quiet (settle_seconds since the room's last noted message) or volume (max_window_messages unjudged messages since the last judged window). The volume arm exists because the quiet arm reads time since the last message and therefore never closes a window in a room whose gaps stay under settle_seconds.

The trigger writes the window watermark and clears the unjudged counter before evaluating, so a closed window is evaluated exactly once even when the gate declines or the turn faults; re-opening it would cost a gate call or a turn on every tick.

The window takes the conversation slot only if it is free, via try_acquire; a held slot means the window is closed and skipped silently before any gate call, because a tag must never wait behind an ambient thought and a stale burst must not be answered after the conversation moved on.
The slot is held across the gate call and the whole participation turn and released in a finally through release_and_dispatch, which starts the next queued tag turn immediately if one is waiting.

note_message is synchronous and called from the dispatcher, which must not await it: it sets the room's message cursor to the trigger's own clock reading rather than the message timestamp, increments the unjudged count, and remembers the conversation type, deferring all evaluation to close_due_windows.

The trigger's retained state is five per-room cursors keyed by (platform, conversation_id), bounded only by sweep, which the runtime loop calls each tick with a one-day TTL on a two-second clock rather than the trigger calling it itself.

The Relevance Gate is admission control and nothing else: one call whose only inputs are the room's transcript window and its standing, with no tools, doctrine, loop or drafting, because its question is whether the window is worth a reply from anyone while whether Nora holds something to add belongs to the turn behind it.

The gate's two visible blocks, group_transcript and standing, are declared as a data table and rendered by a function that can only produce a closed set, so a third block would be caught by a test rather than silently widening the gate's input.

The gate's prompt keeps the instruction in the system role and the room in the user role, and escapes each transcript body inside its own element, so a member typing a forged [assistant]: line cannot occupy a role the operator's rules do not.

GateVerdict.score is reference only and absent rather than zero: it reaches the participation turn as a note in its header and onto the trace, and is never compared against a threshold, because the verdict is the only enforcement surface.

Every non-answer from the gate fails closed to no_go under one of the enumerated GATE_ERROR_KINDS, which is also the metric's label vocabulary, and a finish_reason of "length" is never parsed because a cut-off JSON body can still parse into something shorter and wrong.

The gate refuses two substitutions that would let an outage read as a healthy gate: an unreadable transcript returns no_context instead of an empty prompt the model could answer either way, and a missing or bodyless participation.md returns no_instruction instead of a criteria-free verdict reported as source=model.

GateVerdict.source keeps a chosen no_go apart from a fail-closed one: nora_relevance_gate_total moves only on a real verdict while nora_relevance_gate_errors_total carries the failure kind, both labelled with conversation_id so a refusal can be joined to what she held for that room.

RelevanceGate.decide promises never to raise and never to hang: the model call is bounded inside _ask by call_timeout_seconds, mirroring [relevance_gate] timeout_seconds, because the trigger holds the room's slot across the call and walks its due windows serially; the timeout is counted apart from call_failed and the latency series is observed on every exit.

The gate's verdict is formed on a raw json_object completion with no tools and no declared tool_choice, not on the SDK's structured output, because that transport is measured to believe a forged assistant row — a false GO there is an unauthenticated turn — and the property is enforced by a test that discovers every RelevanceGate construction under nora/ and fails if its client reaches ask_structured.

Passing the poster is what makes gate shadow mode: a GO is posted for review under audience relevance-gate-shadow and no turn runs, the slot is still taken so the reviewed GO rate cannot exceed what the live path could produce, and a reviewed GO never spends the send cooldown.

The cooldown caps sends rather than evaluations: every closed window is evaluated, and send_permitted is derived from an absent-or-expired last send and enforced in the Deliverer after every guard has measured the text and before the audit row and the wire, so a held message leaves no trace in the room and the turn still answers SILENT.

Only a delivered send spends the cooldown: the trigger stamps the in-memory send cursor on the same tick and then attempts the store write, so a held, silent or failed turn leaves the cadence untouched even if persistence fails.

The five cursors are split three ways across a restart: last window end and last send are stored, last message at and conversation type are re-derived at hydration from messages, and the unjudged counter is deliberately neither and restarts at zero, because a messages-derived count would close windows earlier than the live trigger does.

Hydration runs once per process on the first close_due_windows and uses setdefault, so a message noted before the first tick is never rewound, and _hydrated is set only after the read returns so a failed read costs one tick and is retried rather than evaluating against half a cursor set.

Persistence is a mirror, not an input: the store is an optional narrow three-verb protocol read once per process, read_cursors joins the watermark with the newest inbound non-Nora, non-hidden message in one statement, and a failed write is logged without changing what the trigger decides.

record_window_end is an upsert that deliberately does not touch last_send_at, while record_send supplies last_window_end_at on insert, so a close that ran no turn or stayed silent leaves the cooldown intact and a zero-row update cannot silently lose it.

participation_occasion builds an Event with person_id=None and body="" because the quiescence trigger owes the turn to no one person, so the whole basis for the determination is the injected context and the header's stated right to decline.

tests/integration/test_ambient_loop_positive_control.py drives the real ingest, policy, gate, trigger and fire stages with only the models and the platform faked, and asserts the gate was asked exactly once — so a trigger with gate=None could not make the decide stage pass vacuously.
